summary:
ARES (Advanced Reconnaissance & Exploration System) is an interactive planetary terrain intelligence platform that helps explore and assess the Martian surface using real NASA HiRISE Digital Terrain Model (DTM) data from Gale Crater.

ARES transforms high-resolution elevation data into an interactive 3D terrain environment with four scientific visualization layers: elevation, hillshade, slope, and terrain hazard classification. Users can inspect individual terrain locations to retrieve elevation, slope, and geographic coordinates. The platform also features an experimental A* rover route planner that identifies a possible path between selected locations while accounting for terrain steepness and invalid data regions.

By combining planetary science, geospatial processing, 3D visualization, and pathfinding, ARES makes complex Mars terrain data more accessible and demonstrates how terrain intelligence can support preliminary rover exploration and mission planning.
details: Project Overview ARES (Advanced Reconnaissance & Exploration System) is a planetary terrain exploration and intelligence platform developed to make real Martian surface data interactive, understandable, and useful for preliminary rover route assessment. The project uses NASA's High Resolution Imaging Science Experiment (HiRISE) Digital Terrain Model (DTM) data from Gale Crater on Mars. The elevation dataset is processed into scientific terrain products and rendered as an interactive 3D landscape. How It Works ARES combines geospatial data processing, terrain visualization, and pathfinding through the following capabilities: 1. Interactive 3D Mars Terrain - Reconstructs the Gale Crater study area using real NASA elevation data. - Allows users to explore the Martian landscape in a 3D environment. 2. Scientific Terrain Visualization - Elevation: displays terrain height variation. - Hillshade: reveals surface relief and topographic features. - Slope: visualizes terrain steepness. - Hazard Classification: categorizes terrain into gentle, moderate, steep, and very steep regions. 3. Precision Terrain Inspection Users can select a location on the 3D terrain and retrieve its corresponding elevation, slope, and geographic coordinates, enabling detailed investigation of individual terrain locations. 4. Experimental Rover Route Planning ARES implements an A* pathfinding algorithm to generate a possible route between selected locations. The planner considers terrain slope, invalid data regions, and movement costs while avoiding excessively steep areas and preventing diagonal corner-cutting. 5. Mission Assessment The system presents route information, including estimated distance, average slope, maximum slope, and a slope profile to help users evaluate the generated path. Benefits and Intended Impact Martian terrain can be complex and difficult to interpret from raw scientific datasets. ARES makes this information more accessible through an interactive environment that connects scientific terrain analysis with visual exploration. The platform demonstrates how elevation data, terrain classification, and computational pathfinding can be combined to support preliminary rover mobility studies, educational exploration, and future planetary mission-planning research. It can help students, researchers, and space enthusiasts understand how surface conditions may influence exploration decisions. Creativity and Innovation ARES brings together real planetary elevation data, interactive 3D reconstruction, multiple scientific visualization layers, location-based terrain inspection, and algorithmic route planning in one integrated platform. Rather than presenting terrain data only as static maps, ARES allows users to explore the landscape, investigate individual locations, identify potentially challenging terrain, and experiment with rover route generation. Technology and Tools - Frontend: React, TypeScript, Vite - 3D Visualization: Three.js, React Three Fiber, React Three Drei - Backend: Python, FastAPI - Geospatial Processing: Rasterio, GDAL, NumPy - Pathfinding: A* search algorithm - Communication: Axios - Data: NASA HiRISE Digital Terrain Model (Gale Crater) Factors and Limitations Considered The system considers terrain slope, elevation, invalid or NoData raster regions, physical grid spacing, and movement costs during route generation. The route planner is an experimental terrain-based model. Its output is not a certified rover navigation route and does not account for every real-world mobility constraint, rover engineering limitation, or mission safety requirement. Use of AI Assistance ChatGPT was used as an AI-assisted development and writing tool during the project. It supported implementation guidance, code suggestions, debugging assistance, and documentation drafting. The project was assembled, tested, and evaluated through the team's development work. AI assistance is disclosed here in accordance with the challenge requirements.
